answer:
No. You are not supposed to be taking lisinopril any more. Dr. Marsh stopped it on September 22, 2025 because it gave you a dry cough, and switched you to losartan 50 mg once a day. At your December 9, 2025 follow-up the cough had gone. Lisinopril is now also on your allergy and intolerance list as a cause of dry cough.

The app is showing an old record. The copy of your records that still lists lisinopril as active was exported in June 2025, before the change. Every record from September 2025 onward, from your clinic, the hospital and the pharmacy, shows it as stopped or doesn't mention it.

Please don't restart it, and don't take it together with losartan. Both drugs act on the same blood pressure pathway. Taking them together isn't recommended because it can raise potassium and strain the kidneys. If you still have old lisinopril tablets at home, set them aside and ask your pharmacist about disposing of them.

The pharmacy record shows losartan filled on June 28, 2026 for 90 days. It shows no lisinopril fills after the switch. I can't see what is in your medicine cabinet, so if you ever took lisinopril after September 2025, tell Dr. Marsh.

The same kind of out-of-date listing may apply to hydrochlorothiazide. The hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 after you were admitted with low sodium. But the pharmacy filled it on April 2, 2026, your clinic list and the eye clinic list still show it as active, and your sodium was slightly low (134) on June 15, 2026. The records don't tell me whether you are still taking it. Please check this with Dr. Marsh soon.
short: Lisinopril 10 mg was stopped on 2025-09-22 because of a dry cough and replaced by losartan 50 mg daily; the app is showing an outdated June 2025 record, and lisinopril should not be restarted.

knowledge.says: A persistent dry cough is a well-known side effect of ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril, and it usually fades within weeks of stopping. Switching to an ARB such as losartan is the usual alternative because it controls blood pressure without causing that cough.
knowledge.guideline: ACC/AHA hypertension guideline: an ARB is recommended for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE inhibitor because of cough.

knowledge.guideline: ONTARGET trial and ACC/AHA hypertension guideline: do not combine an ACE inhibitor with an ARB.
